newsitem.title: JAPAN: NTT says int'l procurement policy won't change.
newsitem.headline: NTT says int'l procurement policy won't change.

text.p: Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp said on Wednesday that its international procurement policy will not change even if the 1980 Japan-U.S. agreement on NTT's procurement is terminated.
"We feel the government agreement is not necessary," NTT president Junichiro Miyazu told a news conference.
"Even if the agreement is terminated, the volume of our international procurement will not change," Miyazu said.
Miyazu said he does not think U.S. companies have serious complaints about NTT's procurement policy.
He said NTT has not decided on its procurement system after its realignment in 1999, which will split the telecom giant into three units under a holding company.
Telecommunications industry sources said the U.S. government has asked Japan to start negotiations on the renewal of the Japan-U.S. agreement on NTT's procurement on July 21 in Seattle.
The current agreement will expire at the end of September.
